as -sībĭlo (ads- ), āre, v. n. and
I.a., to hiss, murmur, whisper at or to a thing (only in the post-Aug. poets): alno adsibilat alnus, Claud. Nupt. Hon. et Mar. 68; id. Rapt. Pros. 2, 225: “moto adsibilat aëre ventus,” Aus. Mos. 258 .—As verb act.: “serpens animam adsibilat aris, i. e. sibilando amittit,” Stat. Th. 5, 578 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
